definitions.name: \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\)
definitions.construction: Deterministically split \(D_n\) into blocks \(D_\pi,D_\mu,D_*\) of size at least \(m\). On \(D_\pi\) and \(D_\mu\), release once per block the concatenated tensor-spline Gram and moment vector by the Gaussian mechanism with its exact joint \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity, solve the ridged normal equations, and post-process by metric projection onto \(\mathcal H^\alpha(L_\pi;\mathcal X)\cap[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(\mathcal H^\beta(L_\mu;\mathcal X)\cap[0,1]\). Conditional on these pilots, form on \(D_*\) the concatenation of all clipped linear and order-two \(U\)-statistic moment entries \((\widehat Q,\widehat R)\) in the Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman higher-order local \(R\)-learner using \(\rho_h\), \(b_{h,k}\), and the known uniform design; release this concatenation once by the Gaussian mechanism, spectrally clip \(\widehat Q\) below \(\kappa(1-\kappa)/4\), and return \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)=\rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\widehat R_{\mathrm{DP}}\). Each of the three disjoint-block mechanisms receives budget \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\); the released interval is post-processing.

definitions.name: \(B(h,k)\)
definitions.construction: \(B(h,k)=C_B\{h^\gamma+(h/k^{1/d})^q+h^\gamma(h/k^{1/d})^\alpha\}\), where \(C_B\) depends only on the displayed class radii, overlap, and dimension.

definitions.name: \(S(h,k,\eta)\)
definitions.construction: \(S(h,k,\eta)=C_S\sqrt{\frac{\log(8/\eta)}{m h^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{m h^d}\right)}\), where \(C_S\) depends only on the displayed class radii, overlap, and dimension.

definitions.name: \(G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)
definitions.construction: \(G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)=C_G\frac{\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)\log(8/\eta)}}{m\epsilon_n}\{h^{-d}+k h^{-2d}\}\), the Gaussian quantile obtained from the joint sensitivity of the clipped linear and order-two moment vector after spectral stabilization.

definitions.name: \(r_{\mathrm{up}}\)
definitions.construction: \(r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s))}\) if \(s<\frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\) otherwise; \(r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\), \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-q\gamma/\{(d+q)\gamma+qd\}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{up}}=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}\).

definitions.name: the positive-density confidence-modulus handle
definitions.construction: Derive the replacement-private modulus for honest pointwise CATE intervals by combining a coverage-to-testing reduction on ordinary positive-density Hölder bump submodels with a propose-test-release or disjoint-pair-block stabilization of the localized quadratic score, treating the global-sensitivity term of \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\) as the benchmark to improve or certify.

statements.statement: For every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), the Hölder versions are unique on the positive anchor neighborhood and \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0)=\mu_{1,Q}(x_0)-\mu_{0,Q}(x_0)\).
statements.justification: The target must be a point-identified causal contrast rather than an arbitrary version of an almost-everywhere conditional mean.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 uses the observed CATE regression; this lemma records the causal-version equality at the anchor under the present full-data model.
statements.consumer: Applied users can interpret coverage of \(C_n(h,k)\) as coverage of the causal CATE at the prespecified covariate profile \(x_0\).

statements.statement: The concrete attainable model satisfies \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\); its uniform design gives \(\underline f\le f_Q\le\overline f\), and the population localized spline and Legendre Gram matrices have eigenvalues bounded away from zero and infinity uniformly in admissible \((h,k)\).
statements.justification: This inclusion makes the upper theorem a genuine result on a fixed positive-density submodel rather than an estimator-defined class.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 states high-level Gram and density-pilot conditions; the proposition verifies them directly for a named uniform-design submodel.
statements.consumer: The inclusion supplies an auditable benchmark for implementations that randomize or reweight enrollment to an approximately uniform local design.

statements.statement: For replacement-adjacent samples, \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\) and \(C_n(h,k)\) are \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private. The accountant is parallel composition across \(D_\pi,D_\mu,D_*\), one joint Gaussian mechanism within each block, and post-processing thereafter. There is a constant \(C_\Delta\), depending only on the fixed class radii, overlap, and dimension, such that conditional on the projected pilots the main joint moment release has \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity at most \(C_\Delta m^{-1}(h^{-d}+k h^{-2d})\), uniformly over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
statements.justification: Every pilot and every higher-order moment is protected under one explicit replacement-privacy accountant.
statements.gap: SchroederMelnychukFeuerriegel2025 privatizes ordinary orthogonal CATE learners; it does not bound the sensitivity of a localized quadratic correction with shrinking bandwidth and growing basis dimension.
statements.consumer: Privacy officers can audit the release ledger without treating nuisance fits or the quadratic correction as unprotected preprocessing.

statements.statement: There are constants \(C_B,C_S,C_G\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\), such that for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), every \(h\le r_0\), and every \(1\le k\le m h^d\) with \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), the projected private pilots satisfy the same Hölder-radius restrictions as the primitive nuisances and \(\Pr_Q\{|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|>B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\}\le\eta\). The three displayed summands respectively bound localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation of the linear and degenerate terms, and all propagated Gaussian release noise.
statements.justification: A uniform error envelope prevents coverage from being inferred by simply adding a Gaussian variance to a biased nonregular estimator.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 gives an expected-error decomposition without privacy or coverage; ArmstrongKolesar2020 treats worst-case smoothing bias without causal higher-order nuisance bias.
statements.consumer: The bound gives investigators a finite-sample radius that remains valid when low nuisance smoothness makes first-order CATE intervals undercover.

statements.statement: For every admissible \((h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu)\), the released set \(C_n(h,k)\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private and satisfies \(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}\Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta\). Coverage probability integrates the sampling law, all pilot and moment Gaussian noises, and the deterministic sample split.
statements.justification: The headline converts a fully privatized higher-order CATE learner into an honest pointwise causal interval.
statements.gap: SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 proves a private interval for the regular population ATE, while no located theorem gives uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage with higher-order nuisance bias.
statements.consumer: A hospital can release a confidence interval for the treatment effect at a prespecified clinical profile while protecting every patient record.

statements.statement: Choose \((h,k)\) by deterministic minimization of \(B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) over \(h\le r_0\), \(1\le k\le m h^d\), and \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\). For any deterministic pilot spline dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\), \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}\mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}]\le C_L r_{\mathrm{up}}\) for a constant \(C_L\) depending only on the fixed class radii, overlap, dimension, and noncoverage level. Thus the expected length is governed, up to fixed logarithmic factors, by the maximum of the KBRW privacy-free term, the \(\gamma\)-smooth private-regression term, and the explicitly derived global-sensitivity higher-order term; no matching full-class lower claim is made.
statements.justification: The result gives the first auditable privacy phase diagram for the length, rather than only asymptotic validity of a private causal interval.
statements.gap: ShohamEtAl2026 gives a black-box asymptotic resampling interval, and SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 gives a regular ATE interval; neither derives a pointwise Hölder CATE expected-length phase.
statements.consumer: Study designers can select bandwidth, higher-order dimension, and privacy budget to meet a prespecified interval-width requirement.

statements.statement: When the Gaussian release noises are set to zero and the privacy constraint is removed, minimizing \(B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\) yields \(r_{\mathrm{np}}\), including the KBRW elbow at \(s=\frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}\).
statements.justification: The construction must collapse to the established privacy-free higher-order CATE rate in the standard special case.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 establishes this rate for point estimation; this proposition verifies that the bias-aware interval radius preserves it on the attainable submodel.
statements.consumer: Analysts can recover the nonprivate pointwise benchmark continuously as confidentiality constraints are removed.

statements.statement: Let \(\widetilde C_n\) be any replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private interval with \(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}\Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in\widetilde C_n\}\ge1-\eta\). If \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), then \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}\mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(\widetilde C_n)]\ge c\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}\). The lower bound uses only a randomized-treatment, uniform-design, positive-density regression submodel and contains no \(q<\gamma\) paired-cell branch.
statements.justification: This theorem separates the sound full-class privacy limitation from the stronger attainable-submodel upper result.
statements.gap: Existing private pointwise regression bounds concern noncausal regression experiments; the theorem embeds that barrier into honest causal intervals on the unchanged positive-density class.
statements.consumer: Reviewers and privacy-budget committees obtain a defensible lower benchmark without relying on the rejected paired-microcell transport argument.

statements.statement: What is the exact minimax expected-length frontier for replacement-private, uniformly honest intervals for \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\) over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\)? In particular, can the positive-density confidence-modulus handle reduce the higher-order release sensitivity while retaining the uniform bias guarantee, or can it certify that an additional nuisance-driven privacy term is unavoidable?
statements.justification: The gap between the ordinary full-class lower bound and the constructive higher-order upper phase is the genuine unresolved mathematical content.
statements.gap: Neither KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 nor the located private CATE and private confidence-interval papers characterize this privacy-constrained confidence modulus.
statements.consumer: A resolution determines whether private heterogeneous-treatment-effect studies pay only the ordinary local-regression privacy price or an irreducible higher-order nuisance price.

sampling_model.design: Independent observations from \(P_Q\), with a deterministic three-way sample split and known uniform covariate design on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with conditional ignorability and \(\kappa\le\pi_Q(x)\le1-\kappa\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform overlap is fixed over \(\mathcal X\); the full class also has a positive density band around \(x_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Private tensor-spline sufficient-statistic releases for \(\pi_Q\) and \(\mu_{0,Q}\), followed by Hölder-ball projection; a separate block supplies the privatized linear and quadratic local moments.
sampling_model.privacy: Replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differential privacy under parallel composition across disjoint blocks, a single joint Gaussian release within each block, and post-processing for stabilization and interval formation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The higher-order local-polynomial learner attains the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate under its regularity conditions.
Worst-case bias-aware local-polynomial confidence intervals are honest and shrink at the optimal nonparametric rate.
A doubly robust uniform confidence band is constructed for a lower-dimensional CATE function under nonprivate sampling.
DP-CATE preserves Neyman orthogonality asymptotically and gives quasi-oracle conditions for private two-stage CATE learners.
Theorem 4.6 constructs a valid private interval for the population ATE from private point and variance estimates.
A black-box resampling framework converts a private estimator into an asymptotically valid and tight nonparametric confidence interval.

tldr: The project constructs a replacement-private, finite-sample honest confidence interval for pointwise CATE on a concrete uniform-design, positive-density KBRW-attainable submodel. A fully private higher-order local learner uses projected private spline pilots and one joint Gaussian release of its localized linear and quadratic moments. The interval radius displays three separate contributions: Hölder localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation, and propagated privacy noise. Deterministic tuning yields an expected-length upper phase with the privacy-free KBRW term, an ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth private-regression term, and a global-sensitivity higher-order term. On the unchanged full positive-density class, only the sound ordinary regression lower limitation is asserted; the exact nuisance-sensitive private confidence modulus remains open.

project_justification.gap: Private CATE papers provide point releases or quasi-oracle guarantees, and private causal interval papers treat regular average effects. They do not give a uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage theorem that accounts simultaneously for higher-order nuisance bias, sampling uncertainty, privacy composition, and privacy noise.
project_justification.niche: A bias-aware fixed-length construction on a fixed KBRW-attainable positive-density submodel permits honest nonregular causal inference without assuming the desired coverage or length and without relying on the rejected paired-microcell lower bound.
project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment under a blockwise accountant, proves a uniform finite-sample remainder inequality, derives a phase-sensitive expected-length upper bound, and separates it from an ordinary full-class lower limitation and an explicit sharpness question.

related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) provide the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate and the higher-order local-polynomial learner whose bias and variance architecture is retained here. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the quadratic correction. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias rather than estimating it. Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) obtain nonprivate doubly robust CATE confidence bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) establish private Neyman-orthogonal CATE learning and explicitly identify privatization-induced uncertainty as unresolved, but do not derive a pointwise Hölder coverage or length phase. Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) construct private intervals for the regular population ATE; their influence-function variance calculation does not cover localized higher-order CATE bias. Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give a general asymptotic resampling conversion from private estimators to intervals; the present target instead requires uniform finite-sample Hölder bias control and an explicit expected-length phase. Dwork and Roth (2014) supply the Gaussian mechanism, parallel composition, and post-processing facts used by the privacy accountant.
technical_internal_limitation: The displayed higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+k h^{-2d})\) of a direct clipped quadratic-moment release. It is an attainable upper-bound cost, not a minimax lower bound. The proposal does not revive the invalid \(q<\gamma\) paired-microcell transport construction and does not claim that this term is unavoidable on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).
honest_scope: Settled targets are the construction, replacement-privacy accountant, uniform bias and concentration envelope, honest coverage, attainable-submodel expected-length upper phase, privacy-free reduction, and ordinary full-class regression lower limitation. The exact full-class minimax expected-length frontier, including whether higher-order nuisance privacy creates an additional unavoidable branch, is the open-ended question.
novelty_justification: The closest private causal interval result, SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025, concerns a root-\(n\) population ATE and adds privatization uncertainty to an influence-function variance. The closest private CATE result, SchroederMelnychukFeuerriegel2025, provides point learners and quasi-oracle conditions without intervals. The proposed contribution is different in mathematical object and proof route: a finite-sample honest interval for a nonregular pointwise Hölder CATE whose radius exposes higher-order nuisance bias and localized quadratic sampling error, with a replacement-private composition proof and an optimized expected-length upper phase. ShohamEtAl2026 does not subsume this claim because its black-box resampling theorem is asymptotic and does not derive the uniform KBRW-class bias or phase-sensitive length. No exact full-class lower phase is claimed.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: Construct finite-sample replacement-DP honest confidence intervals for the pointwise Hölder CATE at an interior anchor under overlap, bounded common-support outcomes, and positive local design density. On the concrete uniform-design attainable subclass, build a fully private higher-order local learner with privatized nuisance pilots and localized linear and quadratic moments; prove an unrestricted-finite-rank remainder bound, a transcript-wise nonempty clipped interval, and an optimized expected-length upper phase separating privacy-free, ordinary private-regression, and higher-order global-sensitivity terms. On the unchanged full class, prove the ordinary γ-smooth honest-length lower bound and the fixed-dimensional β-smooth private direct-regression upper bound, and state the resulting nonsharp full-class and attainable-class brackets, including a public selector between the two attainable upper constructions. Keep the exact full-class nuisance/private-Gram confidence frontier open; no matched full-class phase is claimed.
